title: dlopen/dlsym/dlclose (dlfcn.h) causes memory leak
body_html:
When using the dlfcn family like so:

#include <stdio.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>

typedef int(*timefunc_t)(void*);

int main()
{
    timefunc_t fun;
    void* handle;
    handle = dlopen("libc.so.6", RTLD_LAZY);
    fun = (timefunc_t)dlsym(handle, "time");
    printf("time=%d\n", fun(NULL));
    dlclose(handle);
    return 0;
}

It causes a Memory leak:

My question is, Is this a programming error, or rather a bug in dlfcn/libdl.so?

events.body_html: Doesn't valgrind already ship with tons of suppression rules that concern dl-type loading? Run it again with -v to see if there's more...

Looks like the latter. However this does not appear to be a big deal because if you repeat the dlopen/dlsym/dlclose calling another routine you'll see that the memory leak is of the same size, it does not grow with the number of dlopen/dlclose calls.
Another way of saying this is that a "O(1) memory leak" is not a leak but a single drop. :-)

jmbr's answer is good, but I'd say it's neither a programming error nor a bug in libdl, just the way things are. There's no advantage to trying to cleanup this memory on exit (since it will be destroyed anyway) and in fact it could lead to bugs in multithreaded code (especially with nasty fork interaction).
